target_customer: Underserved patients and the clinicians and institutions who serve them; funded by philanthropy, partners and investors
problem: Patients lack access to specialist judgment; Human Dx pairs crowdsourced doctor reasoning with machine learning to map the steps to help any patient.
business_model: Public benefit corporation with a companion nonprofit; revenue from partners and grants (Form 990 revenue about $1M in 2016 and 2018)
product_category: Collective medical intelligence and clinical decision support

founders.name: Jay Komarneni
founders.background_notes: MacArthur 100&Change page calls him founder and chair and cites family medical experiences as motivation; education and employers not given.

founders.name: Irving Lin
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page as founder and team member.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a structured system that aggregates clinical reasoning and learns from it required novel data models and later machine learning.

defensibility.rationale: A growing corpus of physician cases and a doctor community are hard to replicate, but rely on sustained clinician participation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; it stayed independent and partnered with the AMA and others per MobiHealthNews headline (not opened).

market_need_then: Diagnostic error and specialist access gaps were known problems; the project later claims thousands of doctors in 60+ countries (MacArthur page).

branding.domain_note: Uses humandx.org, a .org domain, consistent with nonprofit framing

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven; tagline One open system. For all of humankind. (Wellfound listing)

branding.brand_signature: One open system. For all of humankind.
branding.community_and_virality: Doctor community participation, but no independent brand press found.

brand_strength.rationale: Names Human Dx and Human Diagnosis Project are used interchangeably and are generic; credibility came from partners, not the name.

outcome_analysis: Human Dx, formed in 2012, built an open medical intelligence effort with a for-profit entity and a nonprofit. It raised about $2.8M in 2013 per a Form D summary and gathered partners including medical societies. It is still listed active, but sources do not show revenue growth or a clear exit, so its trajectory is stalled or mission driven rather than venture style.
notes: Company website fetch returned no usable content. Funding: Welcome to the Jungle lists $0.2M seed (Dec 2012) and $2.8M (Oct 2013), and says an SEC Form D shows about $2.8M sold to 15 investors; the Form D was not opened, so only the 2013 round is recorded. Union Square Ventures and the Moore Foundation are named as funders there but not tied to a round. Competitor search found Isabel (founded 2000), Figure 1 and Sermo only in undated or later sources, so the list is empty. Outcome searches found no acquisition or shutdown.
